wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up. It rises when Iran does something, or has something done to it, that sends people to a reference work rather than a headline.
wiki-iran.recent: Attention has fallen roughly a third from its 20 July peak even as the war ground on: the strike campaign near the Strait of Hormuz gave way to what Washington calls strangulation, with the UAE suspending all trade and finance with Iran on Wednesday, hours after two ballistic missiles triggered Dubai's first emergency alert in months.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Brent has climbed back toward $93 as the Strait of Hormuz closed commercially: zero vessels transited on Sunday, Kpler data show, and Iran legislated control over the passage rather than declaring a blockade. Trump signaled he won't renew the Iran deal, pushing oil above $91, while a third Greek tanker in three days burned in the Black Sea.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of US light sweet crude, the benchmark American oil is sold against and the reference for fuel prices across North America. It moves on supply and on anything that threatens the routes barrels travel.
wti.recent: The strait did most of the work. Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz, Hormuz traffic fell to single digits as the 60-day deadline for the US-Iran MoU expired, and Trump signaled he won't renew the Iran deal — coverage that put oil above $91 after a Jul 6 low of 69.6. A drone strike also set Libya's Zawiya refinery, its biggest, alight.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub and the reference for American power generation, heating and LNG export contracts. It moves on weather, storage and production, and electricity bills move after it.
natgas-hh.recent: The price has drifted down about 11% over the window, hitting 2.56 on Aug 7 before recovering to 2.79. Nothing in this window explains the fall in supply terms; the gas stories that surfaced were local — a bombing that cut gas to seven towns in Balochistan, a new Pakistani find at Sujawal — none of which touch the American hub this price is set at.

wheat.standing: The world price of milling wheat, quoted per metric tonne, and the reference for bread and flour costs across importing countries. It moves on harvests, export bans and the safety of the sea and river routes grain travels on.
wheat.recent: Grain export infrastructure has been under attack while Europe dries out: Russia hit the rail station at the Danube port of Izmail on 14 August, days after setting Ukraine's largest Danube grain port ablaze, and drought has dropped the Rhine and the Danube low enough to shut a reactor at Cernavoda. The FAO price index reached 131.1.

rice.standing: The world benchmark price for a tonne of milled white rice, the staple grain for roughly half the planet. It moves on monsoon rainfall, export bans and the cost of nitrogen fertiliser, and it lands hardest on import-dependent countries in Asia and West Africa.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen well below its Aug 2024 high of 563.8 even as the Food and Agriculture Organization's broader price index hit 131.1, with heatwaves and wars pushing up other crop costs. Fertiliser remains the swing input: nitrogen is the largest cash cost in smallholder rice farming and its price is set by natural gas markets.

copper.standing: The world benchmark price for refined copper, the metal that carries electricity. Grids, motors, buildings and cables all run on it, so its price is a running tally of how fast the world is electrifying against how fast mines can supply.
copper.recent: Copper sits near its high of $13,550/mt after a 50.79% run, and the input does not explain the move. Zambia, a copper economy, reelected Hakainde Hichilema with 60% of the vote after a campaign fought over the cost of living and a debt restructuring; in Afghanistan, the 2008 Mes Aynak copper deal has produced nothing.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the price at which Washington borrows for a decade and the benchmark that sets mortgage, corporate and emerging-market borrowing costs worldwide. It rises when investors demand more to hold dollars over time.
us-10y.recent: The yield sits near the top of its two-month range, having climbed from 4.38% on Jun 26 to a high of 4.75% on Jul 31. The dollar fell to its weakest since May in early August with a rate hike in doubt, and Trump again moved to fire Fed governor Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies, and the default benchmark for American equities. Trillions in pension and index funds track it, so a company's admission to the list forces those funds to buy the stock.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its high of 7,799 on Aug 13, up 3.3% over the window. The clearest single move came from index mechanics rather than earnings: Reddit rose 11% on the S&P committee's decision alone, with inclusion set for August 18. Jane Street took a $15 billion loss in July as AI stocks slumped.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by a handful of US technology firms, so it moves less with the American economy than with what investors will pay for chips, software and advertising.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near where it started the window, having fallen from its Jun 2 high to a Jul 29 low before recovering. The two months carried heavy news for its largest constituents — Nvidia's disclosed $21 billion SpaceX stake, Apple's removal of several EU App Store fees and its China-cleared AI model, and Meta's superintelligence essay — but none maps onto the swing.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, averaged across US stations and reported weekly. It follows crude oil with a lag, plus refining margins and taxes, and it is the price most households feel first when oil markets move.
us-gas-retail.recent: Drone strikes have been hitting refining capacity across three theatres: Ukraine says two Russian refineries were hit on 6 August, an attack on Nizhnekamsk killed at least 13 on 10 August, and a third drone strike set Libya's Zawiya refinery alight on 11 August. India then cut its windfall tax on petrol and diesel exports to nil on 15 August, adding export supply.

natgas-ttf.standing: The benchmark price of wholesale natural gas in Europe, set at a Dutch virtual trading hub. It is what industry, power stations and home heating ultimately pay for, and it moves on pipeline supply, LNG cargoes and how cold the winter is.
natgas-ttf.recent: The series has climbed roughly 47 percent from its December 2025 low of 9.46, reaching 17.93 in July 2026, its highest point in the window. The input does not identify what drove the rise.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders expect in the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from index option prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear in US equities.
vix.recent: The index has drifted down to the bottom of its three-month range, with the low of 14.25 on Aug 14 well below the 22.22 peak on Jun 10. The same calm shows up elsewhere: Bitcoin volatility nearly vanished in early August as ETFs took in $754 million, and global equities hit record highs. Nothing in the window explains the June spike.

fx-pkr.standing: The exchange rate of Pakistan's rupee against the US dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel, edible oil and machinery in dollars, so the rate sets the domestic price of imported energy and food and the cost of servicing external debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat over the past month, trading in a narrow band between 278.2 on Jul 22 and 276.6 on Jul 31 to sit at 277.2. Nothing in the record explains a move of that size, because there was not one — the pressure showed up in prices rather than the rate, with diesel at 383.95 rupees a litre and gold at $4,392 an ounce.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the US dollar, set on a market-determined float since 2023. Nigeria imports most refined fuel and much of its food, so the naira's level passes through to prices for its 200-million-plus population.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed to 1350 to the dollar, a 2.2% gain over the month from its 1381 high on 22 July, with the low set on 19 August. Nothing in the record explains the move.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency, quoted as pounds per US dollar, so a higher number means a weaker pound. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel, and the rate sets what food, energy and dollar debt service cost the state and the household.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has traded in a narrow band, from 51.37 on Jul 25 to 49.56 on Aug 8 and 50.5 now, a move of about a percent across the month. Nothing in the period explains it: the news from Cairo has been the Gaza mediation, the Warraq Island evictions and the Türkiye defence pact talks, none of which touch the currency.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira's exchange rate against the US dollar. Turkey runs a large import bill in dollars, so the rate feeds directly into domestic fuel, food and input prices, and into the cost of servicing foreign-currency debt.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh low of 47.94 on Aug 19, extending a steady 1.6% slide over the month with no single break. Ankara's month has been busy — the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a law on PKK disarmament, and the transfer of 70 long-range US missiles to Ukraine via Turkey — but none of it shows up as a step in the rate.

fx-bdt.standing: The taka is Bangladesh's currency, quoted here as taka per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker taka. It prices the garment exports that dominate the country's earnings and the fuel and food it buys abroad.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka firmed from 124 on 7 August to 122, a move of about one percent across the month. Nothing in the window explains it: the Bangladesh news of those weeks was political, with ex-PM Hasina calling for the ban on her party to be lifted and India denying involvement in her planned speech.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate of Indonesia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rupiah per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker rupiah. It is the price at which Southeast Asia's largest economy trades its commodity exports and services its dollar debt.

fx-lbp.standing: The street value of Lebanon's currency against the dollar, after a collapse that wiped out most of its worth. Almost everything in the country is priced against it, so households, salaries and savings track it directly.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has held near flat for the month, moving in a narrow band between 89,180 on Jul 31 and 89,720 on Aug 7. That stability held through renewed Israeli strikes in Lebanon — seven killed near Ansar on Aug 15, eleven reported by officials on Aug 17 — and stalled talks in Rome.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the US dollar, managed within a band the central bank sets each morning. It prices the world's largest exporter's goods, so a weaker yuan makes Chinese cars, machinery and electronics cheaper everywhere they land.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted stronger, from 6.775 on 24 July to 6.742, a move of well under half a percent. Nothing in the month's China news explains it: retail sales rose just 0.6% in July, a record 540,000 EVs left the country last month, and Washington accused Beijing of evading tariffs — none of which moved the rate.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar, the rate at which India settles its oil imports, its exports and its remittances. A weaker rupee raises the domestic cost of every barrel and chip the country buys in.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee has traded in a narrow band, easing from 96.5 on Jul 24 to 95.72, with the domestic news flow largely fiscal and political rather than external. Retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June, and India zeroed its petrol export tax while ordering 21 refiners to meet state-set cooking-gas quotas.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker real. It prices Latin America's largest economy — its commodity exports, its dollar-denominated debt and the carry trade that funds both.
fx-brl.recent: The real has drifted about 2.4% weaker over the past month, reaching 5.222 per dollar on Aug 15 after a low of 5.068 on Jul 23. The month's Brazil news ran to policy rather than macro: Petrobras detected signs of oil off the Amazon coast, the central bank ordered exchanges to delay large crypto transfers abroad, and Brasília ordered Discord to suspend livestreams. None of that explains the currency's move.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate of Mexico's peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports north, so the peso prices the trade, remittance and manufacturing ties binding the two economies.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened through the window, touching 17.00 on Aug 17 after a July 24 high of 17.52. The month's Mexico news ran to security and diplomacy rather than macroeconomics: Washington cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa, drawing a rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum, and offered $25 million for a cartel leader as the Sinaloa Cartel split in two.

fx-eur.standing: The euro's exchange rate against the US dollar, quoted here as euros per dollar. It is the world's second-most-held reserve currency, and the rate sets the cost of European exports, imported energy and dollar-denominated debt across the bloc.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted lower through the month, slipping from 0.8792 per dollar on Jul 26 to 0.8633 on Aug 17. Nothing in the period's news explains the move: the EU's activity was regulatory rather than monetary, from the autumn Russia sanctions package to France's telemarketing and social-media rulings.

fx-jpy.standing: Japan's currency, quoted as yen per dollar, and one of the world's most traded. A higher number means a weaker yen, which lifts the earnings of Japan's exporters and raises the cost of the energy and food the country imports.

fx-rub.standing: The ruble's exchange rate against the dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker ruble. It prices Russia's imports and is the most visible gauge of how sanctions, oil revenue and war spending are landing on the domestic economy.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened about 8% over the month to 85 per dollar on 18 August, its low for the period. The EU is preparing its broadest sanctions package yet, which Kallas says have already cost Russia over €1 trillion, while Kyrgyzstan liquidated 19 more companies and cut off over 140 others to avoid secondary sanctions — closing re-export channels Moscow relies on.

fx-zar.standing: The South African rand, quoted as rand per US dollar, is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies and a liquid proxy for risk appetite toward Africa. It moves on metals prices, US rates and domestic politics.
fx-zar.recent: The rand has firmed about 1.3% over the past month, from 16.83 on 25 July to a low of 16.15 on 8 August, and sits at 16.25. The month's South African news ran to governance and security — 70 people killed in a week in Cape Town, R5.1 billion improperly disbursed to 40,000 students — without a single event the series can be pinned to.

btc.standing: The first and largest cryptocurrency, traded around the clock on exchanges worldwide with no central issuer. Its price sets the tone for the rest of the digital-asset market, and increasingly for the ETFs, miners and listed treasuries that hold it.
btc.recent: The drift lower came alongside a market that has stopped tracking equities: bitcoin sits 49% below its record while the S&P 500 hits all-time highs. A $120 million Coldcard hack in early August congested the mempool with the attacker's own transactions, and Russia banned Moscow bitcoin mining until 2032. Volatility collapsed even as ETFs took in $754 million.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency and the settlement asset of the Ethereum network, where most stablecoins, tokenised assets and decentralised trading are issued. Its price is a proxy for demand to use that network, not just to hold the coin.
eth.recent: The month's range was narrow — a high of $1,952 on Jul 27 and a low of $1,845 on Aug 2 — while the regulatory frame moved instead of the price. The Senate missed its pre-recess vote window on the Clarity Act, the SEC scrapped its Reg Crypto vote, and the EU's MiCA migration deadline landed on 10 million users.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by allocated gold bullion, so its price tracks an ounce of gold. Gold is what buyers hold when they distrust currencies and rates, which makes it a running measure of confidence in both.
paxg.recent: Gold climbed through August as markets braced for US inflation data, hitting $4,392 an ounce on Wednesday 12 August, a ten-week high, before setting a fresh peak of $4,413 on 18 August. The metal is up roughly 9 percent over the month from its 21 July low of $4,001. KPMG counted Tether's gold bars by hand for the stablecoin issuer's first audit.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A Wikipedia article on the field of machine systems that learn from data. Its daily readership is a rough gauge of when the technology stops being a specialist subject and becomes something the general public goes looking to understand.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership climbed through a fortnight of AI stories reaching ordinary users: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens amid child-death lawsuits, Spotify said it would stop promoting AI-tagged artists, and Amazon was traced scanning and shredding rare books for training corpora. The peak on Aug 14 coincided with the Spotify tagging news and Qwen's 1-million-token model.

wiki-russia.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It is a measure of public attention rather than events, and it rises when something puts the country in front of readers who then go looking for background.
wiki-russia.recent: Attention tracked a week of escalation on both sides of the war. Ukraine launched one of its largest attacks of the war on 16 August, with 822 drones downed over Moscow by Russia's account, and a strike on Koloskovo in Belgorod killed six, including a 14-year-old. Putin then made a first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, and Japan's ambassador was summoned.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a country of some 250 million people. Attention series like this rise when a place enters the news, so the shape of the curve is a rough map of which events reached a global audience.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The peak on 29 July has no explanation in the material available here, and views have since fallen back to about 10,230 a day. The stories running through the window are largely domestic: a court had to order Imran Khan's hospital transfer, diesel rose Rs6.47 to Rs390.42 a litre after a fuel strike was averted by a dealer margin rise, and Google opened its first Pakistan office with Sharif inaugurating it.

wiki-china.standing: Wikipedia's article on China, a daily count of how many people open the encyclopedia's overview of the country. The series tends to move with events rather than interest in the subject itself, so its spikes point to whatever news pulled a general reader toward the basics.
wiki-china.recent: The 13 August peak came in a week dominated by the death of former premier Zhu Rongji at 97, the architect of the reforms most readers were looking up, and by America's accusation that China was evading tariffs. Beijing's coast guard also began patrolling east of Taiwan, and Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy there.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The 33km-wide sea lane between Iran and Oman, the only way out of the Persian Gulf. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil and much of its LNG passes through it, so anything that narrows it prices energy everywhere.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership tracked the strait's closure. Transits fell to zero on Sunday as the US-Iran MoU expired, war-risk premiums and owners' refusals doing the work of a blockade; Trump, who said "we own it," threatened to bomb mediator Oman. The peak on 18 August followed an unknown projectile hitting a vessel's engine room, killing one crew member.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: Pageviews for the Wikipedia biography of the sitting US president — a rough daily gauge of how many people worldwide went looking for background on him, rather than any measure of his approval or activity.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Readership fell to its 30-day low on Aug 15 before recovering: the Aug 11 report that Trump left Ankara hidden inside a catering truck after an Iran threat drove earlier traffic, and the Supreme Court denied his appeal without comment on Aug 17. The Kennedy Center board voted itself past a judge's order on Aug 13.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India, a rough gauge of how much of the world is looking the country up on any given day.
wiki-india.recent: The peak on Aug 15 fell on India's 80th Independence Day, when Modi used the Red Fort address to promise eight more chip plants and nuclear reactors and to declare the decades-old Naxal insurgency finished, and an Army band opened the ceremony with Vande Mataram. Attention has fallen 13.5% since.

wiki-israel.standing: Wikipedia's country article for Israel, and how many people open it each day. Attention here is a rough gauge of how far a story about the state has travelled beyond the region — a proxy for who outside is paying attention.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Wikipedia's article on Ukraine, and how many people read it each day. Attention to a country's basic reference page rises when events force outsiders to look it up, so the curve is a rough gauge of how far a war has travelled beyond the people fighting it.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The month's traffic tracked a widening war rather than a single event: Ukrainian drones killed 13 in Nizhnekamsk on 10 August and hit the Novorossiysk naval base two days later, Russia set Ukraine's largest Danube grain port at Izmail ablaze, and Russia says it downed 822 Ukrainian drones over Moscow in one night. Lavrov rejected freezing the war at today's front line.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Wikipedia pageviews for Nigeria, a daily count of how many people opened the country's encyclopedia entry. Attention on a country of over 200 million people usually spikes on an election, a security incident or an energy story.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Readership tracked Osun state's election: the vote drew live results coverage on 15 August, and Atiku, Obi, Kwankwaso and Saraki congratulated Adeleke on his re-election the next day. Civil society groups tallied 56 incidents and 14 deaths around the ballot, and lawmakers demanded a probe of the violence.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Transits collapsed to zero on Sunday as war-risk insurance, not a blockade, closed the strait; Iran has since legislated a transit statute, and an unknown projectile hit a ship's engine room off Muscat, killing one crew member. Trump threatened to bomb Oman, the mediator, while Adnoc routes crude around Hormuz through Fujairah.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits well below its 90-day baseline as Houthi attacks widened from shipping to Saudi territory: six sailors died in a Bab al-Mandeb strike on a cargo ship, missiles and drones hit the Red Sea port of Mokha, and the Jazan refinery was struck. Maersk raised profit guidance to $6.5 billion on the rerouting.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic remains far below capacity as carriers keep avoiding the Red Sea: the death toll from a Houthi attack on a cargo ship rose to six on 11 August, and Houthi strikes hit Saudi Arabia and an Aramco refinery in Jizan earlier in the month. Maersk, routing around Africa, lifted full-year profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has run near the low end of its 88-day range, at 177 vessels a day, close to the 170 low on 19 July and well below the 266 peak on 27 July. The closure of Hormuz, where transits have fallen to single digits, has cut Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia — removing tanker voyages that would otherwise have run the strait.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic sits about 12% above its 90-day baseline as China presses its claim around the island: the coast guard now patrols east of Taiwan, Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy there, and Jakarta signed on to Beijing's Taiwan line. Typhoon Dolphin cut sailings on 9 August, matching the 28-vessel low.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Daily transits are down about a tenth over the window and 4.5% below the 90-day baseline, sitting at 33 vessels after a 13 July peak of 83 and a 22 July low of 22. The input does not identify what drove the swing.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Turkey began rationing passage in early August, turning back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk, and traffic has fallen to 37 vessels a day, well below the 90-day baseline. Attacks on shipping followed: a third Greek vessel in three days burned in the Black Sea, and TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic sits near its own 90-day baseline, and the swings within the window are routine rather than event-driven — the low of 111 vessels on Jun 3 and the high of 163 on Jun 13 both fall inside normal variation, with calm seas since. The strait's disruptions this summer were on land, not water: the Ceuta crossings and Spain's new checks on the Italian border moved people, not cargo.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic has drifted down through the summer, from 210 vessels a day on May 23 to 126 on Aug 3, with the last week running just under the 90-day baseline. Nothing in the record explains the decline: seas have been calm, with waves peaking at 1.1m.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic is close to its own 90-day baseline after peaking at 123 vessels a day on Jul 31, with rough seas and waves to 3.1m on the current leg. Nothing in the eastern routes has forced a fresh surge: Hormuz traffic fell to single digits in mid-August, but that slowdown has not yet shown up as extra rounding of the Cape.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Vessel movement has stopped: the strait recorded no transits, against a high of 25 a day on Jun 4, and the last week ran 95.7% below its own 90-day baseline. The Black Sea approach has become a shooting gallery — a third Greek vessel in three days burned there, following Ukraine's drone strike on the Russian port of Novorossiysk.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits below its Jun 16 high of 11150 after a run of Houthi strikes on Saudi territory: 12 missiles hit Yemen's oil provinces, a strike on Najran wounded 11, and Aramco put out a fire at its Jizan refinery, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude daily. The Mecca defence pact signed with Turkey and Pakistan on 7 August names no obligations.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits near the top of its 62-day range after a run of Ankara-centred diplomacy: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact in Mecca on 7 August, and parliament passed a Kurdish disarmament law on 10 August. Regional risk cuts the other way — Turkey rationed Bosphorus passage for vessels bound for Novorossiysk.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index has climbed about 5% over the month but fell back Tuesday as the war reached the UAE directly: two Iranian ballistic missiles triggered Dubai's first emergency alert in months, and Abu Dhabi suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Earlier, seven blasts hit Jebel Ali port and two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index reached its high of 1748 on Aug 5, the day before reports that Gulf crude exports to Malaysia had dipped on the Hormuz closure; it has drifted down since as the shortfall reached Malaysian refineries. It stands at 1730, up from 1657 on Jul 1.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index sits at its highest of the 58-day window after a run from June. Prabowo's nomination of a central bank deputy as the new governor on 11 August was the one policy question in the period the market had to price, and the rupiah rose slightly on the news. The 16 August Flores quake, which killed 53, did not register.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index has drifted down about 1% over the past quarter, and the domestic demand picture behind it is weak: China's retail sales rose just 0.6% in July, with households saving rather than spending while the surplus goes out as exports. Corporate news has been about raising cash and capex — Alibaba is selling Lingxi Games to Trustar Capital for $1.5 billion to fund AI spending.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Retail sales rose just 0.6% in July, and the export machine kept absorbing what households would not buy — 540,000 EVs left China last month, a record. Washington accused Beijing of evading tariffs and banned robotics parts, while Alibaba sold Lingxi Games for $1.5 billion to fund AI spending.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index has fallen about a fifth from its 22 June high, with the drop concentrated in memory: SK Hynix dropped 5% on a $38 billion fab bet, and all 2027 memory capacity is already sold out, leaving little room for the AI trade to expand. North Korea resumed missile testing ahead of US-South Korea drills.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index has drifted down from its Aug 6 high of 78,950 to 77,020, a fall of about a fifth of a percent on the day. Policy pressure on domestic consumer and energy sectors ran through the period: New Delhi set output quotas for 21 refiners on cooking gas, weighed ending zero-fee digital payments that banks have subsidised, and faced a challenge from its own adviser to the E20 ethanol mandate.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a fifth from its Jun 10 low of 4,959 to a Aug 17 high of 5,768, then slipped 1.4% in a day to 5,689. The coverage in this window does not explain the move: it runs to a Singapore hardware-wallet breach that leaked 39,798 buyers' addresses, and to Singapore's positioning on Israel.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index sits well below its 22 June high after a 30 July low, and the pressure around it is political rather than commercial: China's coast guard now patrols east of Taiwan, Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy in the same waters, and Jakarta endorsed Beijing's claim. Taiwan also reported an AI-driven hacking campaign.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the top of its 43-day range after climbing from its May 19 low of 1517, with a 1.4% drop on the latest session. The coverage window is dominated by politics rather than markets: Bangkok hosted Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing on 6 August, drawing ASEAN criticism, and a school shooting in Nonthaburi on 7 August killed eight and prompted the prime minister to promise stricter gun laws.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits below its Jul 17 high of 6404 after a 3.9% single-day drop, with the Senate impeachment trial of Sara Duterte grinding through its fourteenth day: witnesses have described confidential funds disbursed to names like Miggy Mango and Jay Kamote, and a P125-million transfer to a security officer.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after the RBA held rates steady on 11 August as the housing market softened, leaving another hike possible. It reached 9,272 on 6 August, then slipped ahead of inflation data. China's steel transition toward scrap recycling weighs on the iron ore demand that anchors the index's largest miners.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index has drifted down about 0.7% over the two months, off the 117,500 high on Aug 7 and above the 108,300 low on Jul 23. Nothing in the record explains the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index has drifted down roughly 6% from its Aug 3 high to close at its lowest level of the window on Aug 18. Petrobras detected signs of oil off the Amazon coast in the Foz do Amazonas basin, and Lula, standing on a Petrobras drillship, called it a passport to the country's future.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down since late May, hitting a 67-day low of 63,930 on Aug 18. Washington cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa on Aug 14, drawing a rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum, and offered $25 million for a Mexican cartel leader — a run of US pressure on Mexico City that has run alongside the slide.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index sits well below its 22 July high of 3,380,000, drifting back toward the 2,775,000 low of 19 May, and fell 1.89% on the day. The 18 August arrest of a Milei adviser over the shooting of lawyer Nadia Beller dominated the Argentine news cycle, but nothing in the record links it to the move.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index sits near its high after climbing through the summer, with the peak on Aug 13 and a floor of 33740 back on May 19. The move is not explained by the Canadian news in view: wildfires that forced 20,000 evacuations in British Columbia, and the unresolved question of whether Canada avoids new U.S. tariffs.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index reached 7,799 on Aug 13 and has drifted down since, closing 0.69% lower at 7,692. Nothing in the past week's US news names a market cause: the Pentagon's $22.9 billion Tomahawk contract with Raytheon and the Army's $10 billion pilot-training deal are defence awards, and China's ban on robotics components has stranded startups rather than large listed firms.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index has climbed about 4% over the window, with the high on Jul 29 and the low on Jun 9. Oil above $91 after Trump signaled he won't renew the Iran deal supports the energy producers that anchor the index, though the input does not explain the wider move.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index reached 26,440 on Aug 14 before easing to 26,130, up about 7 percent over the window. Frankfurt's banks carried much of it: Commerzbank said a tie-up with UniCredit could create value, after Berlin had called the takeover a sovereignty threat. Brussels then set out its broadest Russia sanctions package.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index sits near the top of its 63-day range after climbing from its May low, and the week's news out of France ran to policy and weather rather than earnings: the top court struck down the under-15 social media ban, and jellyfish swarms knocked out 3.2 gigawatts of nuclear power at Gravelines. Neither explains the day's slight decline.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range, up about 9 percent since the 1016 low on May 18 and reaching 1120 on Aug 13 before easing. The material here does not explain the move.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index climbed roughly a fifth over the series to a high of 20210 on Aug 11, holding near that level since. The material here is domestic rather than financial: Spain imposed reciprocal border checks on Italy, and 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta, a city of 84,000. Neither explains the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index climbed roughly 9% over the window to a 53,720 high on Aug 7, with bank consolidation in the frame: Commerzbank said on Aug 6 that teaming up with UniCredit could create value. It has since eased about 1% to 53,020, with no single event in view behind the pullback.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range, up about 9% over the window and roughly a fifth of a percent below the 14,630 high set on Aug 10, after a low of 13,220 on Jun 3. The available material does not explain what drove the climb.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index climbed over the window to a high of 3327 on Aug 5, then drifted back to 3275. Neither the Volkswagen ownership dispute nor Spotify's move to stop promoting AI-tagged artists explains the index level itself.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

wiki-turkey.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Turkey, a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up. Attention series like this spike when a place enters a story big enough to send strangers looking for background.
wiki-turkey.recent: The peak came around the Mecca pact: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a collective-defence agreement on 7 August that names no obligations and never states whose nuclear deterrent applies, with defence chiefs and foreign ministers forming a standing bloc and Egypt staying out. Turkey then passed a Kurdish disarmament law on 10 August.

xag.standing: The price of an ounce of silver, tracked through a token backed one-for-one by physical metal. Silver is both a monetary hedge and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics, brazing — so investment and factory demand pull on it at once.
xag.recent: Silver is up 14.16% across the 31-day window, at 63.29 an ounce. The series ran from a low of 29.80 on Aug 6 to a high of 66.52 on Aug 15, and has eased slightly since.

wiki-venezuela.standing: A daily count of how many people open the Wikipedia article on Venezuela, a rough gauge of how much of the world is looking at the country at once. Attention series like this spike on the days a place makes news and decay quickly after.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia wins the largest bloc of seats at the next State Duma election. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves when the political calendar or the party's grip on it changes.

wiki-osun-state.standing: A state in southwestern Nigeria, in the Yoruba heartland, whose governorship elections are held off-cycle from the national vote and are treated across the country as a read on party strength and on how well the electoral commission's systems hold up.
wiki-osun-state.recent: Osun voted for governor on 15 August, and readership tracked the count: Adeleke led by 67,232 votes after 15 of 30 areas and rivals conceded within a day, with Atiku, Obi, Kwankwaso and Saraki congratulating him. The campaign was violent — civil society groups tallied 56 incidents and 14 deaths — and lawmakers demanded a probe.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at the next meeting. It prices how firmly traders expect the Fed to sit still, and rate expectations set the cost of borrowing, the dollar and the price of every other asset.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The contract has climbed from 39% on Aug 1 to a peak of 75% on Aug 15, settling at 72%. Traders have been pricing the Fed's next tests since CPI, and the bet has firmed alongside a reviving fight over Fed independence after Trump again moved to fire Cook.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether JD Vance wins the 2028 US presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, quoted as a percentage, and it reprices whenever the field of candidates or a contender's standing shifts.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.recent: The series sat at 20% and ends there, having touched 23% on Aug 13 before giving the move back. Nothing in the window explains the swing; the surrounding news about prediction markets concerned the venues rather than the race, with JPMorgan cutting off Polymarket and a federal regulator overriding a New York ban on Kalshi.

wiki-syria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Syria, a proxy for how many people outside the country are trying to understand it. Attention series like this one rise when a place forces itself onto the world's agenda.
wiki-syria.recent: The 11 August peak followed the death sentence passed on Bashar al-Assad in absentia, a verdict 564 outlets carried. Attention returned on 18 August, when Damascus granted the IAEA access to an undeclared Assad-era nuclear site concealed for 18 years, and Israel struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib eight times.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, YouTube and DeepMind, and one of the largest firms on the US market. Its revenue rests mainly on search advertising, so antitrust rulings, app-store remedies and shifts in how people find information all land on the share price.

stocks:ICE.standing: The exchange operator that owns the New York Stock Exchange and the ICE futures markets, where Brent crude and much of the world's energy and interest-rate risk is priced. It earns fees on trading volume, so it profits when markets are volatile.
stocks:ICE.recent: The ticker shares an abbreviation with two unrelated news subjects — Immigration and Customs Enforcement and sea ice — and nothing in this window explains the exchange's share price. The stock rose from $141.6 on Jul 20 to a high of $156.3 on Jul 30, ending at $154.3.
